messages:
Anna K: Heads-up — monitoring just fired a page-retirement alert for GPU 2 on node-39 (eu-west1). gpu.page_retire_count jumped 0 -> 9 in the last 24h.
Miguel: Yep, I see the same in Grafana. Trend for gpu.page_retire_count{node=\"node-39\",gpu=\"2\"} slope is steep; correctable ECC spikes correlate. Screenshot: https://img.redwood/capture/..
Anna K: dmesg excerpt: 
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x23:0xffff:66)
[ 12345.679012] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: GPU 2: Xid 79: GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 12346.100200] NVRM: Correctable ECC error on GPU 0000:65:00
```
Miguel: Xid 79 usually means memory/PCI hiccup. Our HW playbook says: page_retire_count >= 5 OR any uncorrectable ECC -> drain & replace.
Deepa: Remind me — is the retire threshold 5? I remember we moved it to 7 for some older SKUs to reduce churn.
Miguel: Policy doc: default retire_threshold=5 for A100/RTX6000. We bumped to 7 for T4s. This is an A100, so 5 applies.
Anna K: Capacity note: node-39 serves ~8 inference pods, ~10% of eu-west1 inference capacity. If we drain now there will be short spike in tail latency. Any spare capacity in region?
Ryan: We have 2 standby dedicated workers in the region but only 1 is free in prod. If we drain, autoscaler should spin up new pods in eu-west1-b. Expect ~5-10m to rebalance.
Miguel: Commands I ran: 
```
kubectl cordon node-39
kubectl drain node-39 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300 --timeout=10m
```
Deepa: Please annotate the node so ops+hw know intent: `kubectl annotate node node-39 hw/gpu-page-retire=retiring` and add to tracker doc: https://docs.redwood/gpu-fleet-tracker (sheet row for node-39).
monitoring-bot: Alert: gpu.page_retire_count exceeded threshold on node-39 gpu-2 (value=9) at 2026-03-07T09:12:34Z. Related alerts: gpu.ecc.correctable spike, nvml.error.uncorrected_count=0.
Anna K: I'm executing the drain now. Also collecting nvml: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,serial,memory.total,memory.free,ecc.errors.corrected,ecc.errors.uncorrected --format=csv -i 2` and saving /var/log/gpu-diagnostics/node-39-gpu2.log
Miguel: Created vendor ticket INC-5621 with serial S/N ABC12345 and attached nvml + dmesg. Vendor asked for nvml diag & nvml-smi -q output.
Deepa: After drain, let's run vendor memtest on the card once it's in lab or after RMA. If vendor can't RMA same-day, mark GPU as quarantined and schedule replacement in next maintenance window.
Ryan: Tagging @oncall-infra in case the drain causes evictions we don't expect. Also FYI: autoscaler might add a new instance which will draw from reserved pool.
Anna K: Drain completed. Pods evicted and rescheduled. Node-39 now cordoned, annotation set, and I removed from autoscaler group. Evicton CPI: approx 7 pods, capacity impact ~12% for 6 minutes.
Miguel: I bumped alert smoothing from 1m -> 5m to reduce noise on page_retire_count spikes. Also proposing an autosafe rule: auto-drain when page_retire_count >= 10 for sustained 10m OR any uncorrectable ECC >0. Will prepare PR for playbook.
Deepa: Observed Xid 63 earlier as well — DMA parity fault — and Xid 79 later. Co-occurrence suggests either bad DIMM on card or firmware bug in ECC scrub. Please escalate to firmware team if vendor RMA doesn't clear it.
Anna K: Action items I captured in tracker (node-39 row): 1) vendor RMA INC-5621, 2) drain complete & node cordoned, 3) replace card during maintenance window or accept immediate swap if vendor offers spare, 4) run memtest & nvml diag post-replace, 5) update fleet dashboard and ARM capacity planner. I'll post updates here once vendor confirms RMA ETA.
Ryan: :thumbsup: keep this thread updated. If RMA will take >48h, we should consider moving critical tenants to other regions to keep latency SLAs.
Miguel: Also adding a small notebook to correlate page_retire_count, correctable ECC rate, and Xid events across fleet to detect early degraders. Might reduce reactive replacements.
Anna K: Thanks all — closing the operational loop now. Will reopen thread if node status changes or RMA updates arrive.
